summary: A fast, ten-minute hidden-role party game where everyone gets a secret role and character abilities happen once at night, then the whole group argues and votes on who's a werewolf. There's no elimination and no moderator needed, so it plays quickly and repeatedly with large mixed groups.
praised: extremely fast, easy to teach to newcomers
great for large groups and quick repeat plays
clever design lets anyone run it via the companion app with no dedicated moderator
criticised: outcome leans heavily on group bluffing skill and social dynamics rather than strategy
can feel like a coin-flip when players are quiet or new to bluffing
loses novelty after many plays with the same group

interaction.kind: open accusation, bluffing, and group voting
interaction.detail: Players openly discuss, accuse, and defend themselves before a single simultaneous vote decides the outcome, so the entire game is driven by direct verbal interaction. Nearly all information is either shared through discussion or deliberately concealed, with almost no private tableau.

scoring.how_you_win: There is no point score: after one night of secret role abilities, all players vote simultaneously to lynch one player, and whichever team's win condition is met by that outcome (e.g., villagers win if a Werewolf is lynched) wins immediately.
